main_body: Half-timbered house with a large hipped tile roof and a front gable, plus a lower gabled porch bay with a door at the bottom; the chimney is a small detail.
top_band: Roof slope: orange and ochre tile rows with highlight stripes, running from about row 6 down to about row 42 (x=72 column: ridge at rows 0-5, then tile courses). Below it is a dark eave edge and the plaster wall face.
evidence: The roof is drawn as large sloped tile surfaces with visible courses, hips and a front gable, so the top slopes are clearly visible from above. Under the dark eave line the half-timbered wall faces sit set back in shadow. Doors and windows have dark frames. The wall face is a vertical south face. The lower porch bay follows the same construction: a gable roof above its wall and door. It matches the Beodeul house references, so the structure contract is met.

style.evidence: The candidate has 18 median colours per tile, the same as house-h101, and 202 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, like both references. Only 12% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted: dark plum-brown beside the roof tiles and dark brown beside the timber. The roof tiles carry per-tile highlights and several tone steps. The plaster is speckled and the timber has grain. It would sit next to the references without looking thinner or flatter.
